title: Oceans and Continents — Class 6 CBSE Social Science
subject: Social Science

slides.title: Oceans and Continents
slides.speaker_notes: Today we map the big landmasses (continents) and the big bodies of water (oceans).

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
bullets: State the land/water proportions on Earth.
Name the 7 continents in order of size.

slides.title: Land vs Water
bullets: All five oceans are CONNECTED — one 'world ocean'.

slides.title: The seven continents — continued
bullets: Antarctica is COLDEST; Africa has the LARGEST hot desert.

slides.title: Major features by continent
bullets: South America → Amazon rainforest + Andes mountains.

slides.title: The five oceans — by size
bullets: 1. Pacific — largest, deepest. ~30% of Earth's surface.
3. Indian — south of Asia, west of Australia.
5. Arctic — around the North Pole. Smallest.

slides.title: India in the world
bullets: Bay of Bengal east, Arabian Sea west.
Tropic of Cancer through the middle of India.
Most of India in the TORRID heat zone (hot).

slides.title: India's neighbours
bullets: Himalayas to the north — natural barrier.
slides.speaker_notes: Six land neighbours; Sri Lanka and Maldives across the sea.

slides.title: You try (5 minutes)
bullets: 4. Which continent has no permanent population?
5. Order: Africa, Asia, Australia by size.

slides.title: Quick check
bullets: Q4. Continent with the South Pole?

slides.title: World ocean — connected water
bullets: Ships can travel from one ocean to another.

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: 7 continents: Asia, Africa, NA, SA, Antarctica, Europe, Australia.
5 oceans: Pacific, Atlantic, Indian, Southern, Arctic.
Asia is biggest; Pacific is biggest; Antarctica is coldest.
India is in Asia, on the Indian Ocean.
Tropic of Cancer through India → Torrid Zone.
slides.speaker_notes: Hand out worksheet; assign labelled-map homework.
